stem: A startup is building a mobile app that lets small teams share task lists. Users edit lists on their phones, sometimes without a connection, and expect changes to appear on teammates' devices as soon as they reconnect. Each task has different optional fields that the product team keeps changing. Which database fits best?

choices.text: BigQuery, a data warehouse that stores each task update as a row for later analysis with SQL
Firestore, a serverless document database with real-time synchronization and offline support for mobile and web apps
Cloud SQL, a managed relational database that requires a fixed table design defined in advance for every task field and each change
Spanner, a globally consistent relational database for banking-style transactions across regions

stem: A national retailer has ten years of sales, loyalty and web-traffic history, many terabytes in total. Business analysts, who know SQL, want to run complex aggregate reports across all of it, such as revenue by region and product over time. The company does not want to size, tune or maintain database servers. Which service should hold and analyze this data?

choices.text: BigQuery, because it is a serverless data warehouse that analyzes very large datasets with SQL and no servers to manage
Cloud SQL, because analysts can query the whole ten-year history from one managed relational instance that the team sizes and tunes
Bigtable, because key-based lookups on a single sales row return in milliseconds
Firestore, because documents can store each sales record with a flexible set of fields

stem: A new executive asks the data team to explain the difference between relational and non-relational databases in plain terms. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A non-relational (NoSQL) database cannot scale beyond one server and is used only for small applications
A non-relational database requires the same fixed table design as a relational one, only with different software
A non-relational database can store data as documents, key-value pairs or wide columns, often with a flexible schema
A relational database is a type of object storage that keeps each row as a separate file
A relational database stores data in tables with defined relationships and is queried with SQL

stem: A news agency stores millions of photos, video clips and PDF press releases. Reporters upload files from anywhere, editors need to fetch each file by name, and the agency wants capacity that grows without planning and is billed for what it keeps. Nobody needs to run SQL over the files. Which description explains why Cloud Storage suits this need?

choices.text: It is object storage that holds each file as an object in a bucket and scales without capacity planning
It is a relational database that splits each photo into rows and columns for joins
It is a data warehouse that loads every video into a table so that analysts can aggregate frames with SQL
It is a document database that keeps each press release as a JSON record with a flexible set of fields

stem: A company moved last year's customer-support recordings to Archive storage to save money. This quarter the compliance team began reviewing the recordings every week, and the storage bill went up instead of down. What explains the result?

choices.text: Archive storage is a zonal class, so the weekly reviews are charged a cross-region transfer fee each time
Archive storage cannot be read at all until the objects are first moved back to Standard storage
Archive storage costs more per stored gigabyte than Standard storage once data is a year old
Archive is meant for data read less than once a year, so frequent reads add access costs that outweigh savings

stem: A machine learning team trains models on a very large image dataset. The training cluster runs in a single zone, and the team has found that data loading from storage is the bottleneck, leaving expensive accelerators idle. The team wants storage placed in the same zone as the cluster for the lowest possible latency. Which Cloud Storage option is designed for this?

choices.text: Archive storage in a multi-region bucket, which gives the lowest storage cost for large datasets
Coldline storage in a dual-region bucket, which keeps a copy of the data in two regions
Rapid storage in a zonal bucket, which is optimized for I/O-intensive workloads next to compute
Nearline storage with Autoclass enabled, which moves unread data into colder classes over time

stem: A regional bank runs a self-managed MySQL database in its own data center. The hardware lease ends in six months. The bank wants to move to a managed Google Cloud database, keep the application running during the move, and switch over with as little downtime as possible. Which Google Cloud service is designed to help?

choices.text: Looker, which models data so that business users can build dashboards on the old database
Database Migration Service, which handles the initial snapshot and ongoing replication to Cloud SQL for MySQL
Cloud Storage Autoclass, which moves database files between storage classes during the migration
Pub/Sub, which broadcasts each database row as a message that other systems can subscribe to

stem: A mid-sized insurer runs several self-managed databases on virtual machines in its own data center. Its administrators spend most of their week on patching, backups and failover tests. Leadership wants to modernize by moving to managed database services. Which TWO benefits should leadership expect? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Capacity can be adjusted to demand, without buying and installing new hardware for peak load
The insurer gains full control of the physical servers and operating system that run each database
Every application can run unchanged on any managed database, whatever engine it was written for
The insurer is released from all responsibility for who can access its data and how it is classified
Google takes over routine tasks such as backups, patching and failover so staff can focus on applications and data

stem: A small consultancy and a global payments company each need a new relational database. The consultancy's internal tool will serve a few hundred users in one region. The payments company must process transactions from customers on several continents with strong consistency and near-continuous availability. Which pairing of products is the most appropriate?

choices.text: Spanner for the consultancy and Cloud SQL for the payments company
Cloud SQL for the consultancy and Spanner for the payments company
Bigtable for the consultancy and Firestore for the payments company
BigQuery for the consultancy and Cloud Storage for the payments company

stem: A retail company has a central data warehouse, but only a small team of analysts can pull answers from it. Store managers, buyers and marketers wait days for reports, and each department defines "net sales" differently. Leadership wants every employee to explore trusted data on their own, using one shared definition of each metric. Which Google Cloud product addresses this?

choices.text: Spanner, to move the whole data warehouse into a transactional database that every employee can query directly
Pub/Sub, to send each employee a message every time a sales record is created
Cloud Storage, to give every employee access to the raw files that the warehouse is built from
Looker, a BI platform with a semantic layer that sets governed metric definitions for self-service use

stem: A food-delivery company wants its operations team to watch orders, courier locations and delivery delays on a wall dashboard that updates within seconds, so dispatchers can reassign orders before customers complain. Which combination is the most direct way to deliver this?

choices.text: Firestore to store courier data and Dataflow to print a daily summary for dispatchers
Cloud SQL to store all events and a monthly email report generated by an analyst
BigQuery to analyze the continuously arriving data and Looker to present it as live dashboards
Cloud Storage Archive to keep the order events and Spanner to render them on the dashboard

stem: A credit-card company reviews transactions for fraud in a nightly batch job. Fraudsters often make many purchases within minutes, so most losses happen before the next morning's review. Executives ask why the company should invest in real-time streaming analytics. Which TWO statements describe the value? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Streaming analytics works only if the company copies all transaction data into a spreadsheet each night
Events are analyzed as they happen, so suspicious activity can be flagged and acted on within seconds instead of hours
Streaming analytics guarantees that no transaction will ever be fraudulent
Streaming analytics removes the need for any historical data, because only the latest event matters
Decisions and customer experiences can be based on current data, such as blocking a card or sending an alert immediately

stem: A smart-home company has millions of thermostats that send readings continuously. Several teams, such as billing, energy forecasting and device support, each need to consume these readings, and engineers do not want the thermostats to depend on any team's systems being online. Which service decouples the senders from the consumers?

choices.text: Cloud Storage Coldline, a low-cost class that keeps readings for long-term retention
Cloud SQL, a relational database that every team queries directly whenever it needs the latest thermostat reading
Looker, a business intelligence platform that visualizes the readings in dashboards
Pub/Sub, a messaging service where publishers send events to a topic and subscribers receive them

stem: A media company receives clickstream events through a messaging service. It needs to clean the events, remove duplicates, enrich them with customer information and load them into BigQuery, both for a continuous stream and for large historical files. The team wants a fully managed service that scales automatically with the volume and does not require managing servers. Which service fits?

choices.text: Dataflow, a managed service that runs batch and streaming data pipelines and autoscales its workers
Cloud Storage Nearline, a storage class that deduplicates and enriches the files it holds
Firestore, a document database that transforms events as they are written into collections
Looker, a BI platform that cleans and loads data by letting analysts drag fields onto a dashboard

stem: A bank has hundreds of existing data-processing jobs written for Apache Spark and Hadoop that run on its own cluster. Contracts for the hardware end soon. Leadership wants to move these jobs to Google Cloud quickly, keep the open source tools the engineers already know, and avoid paying for an idle cluster between runs. Which Google Cloud service fits?

choices.text: Cloud SQL, which runs Spark code inside the relational engine
Pub/Sub, which executes the jobs on a schedule after each message arrives
Managed Service for Apache Spark, which runs open source Spark and Hadoop jobs on clusters started and stopped on demand
Looker, which automatically rewrites the existing Spark code into dashboards that business users can open and share

stem: A company has two data projects. Project one is a new pipeline that must process events from a message stream and also handle historical files, with no servers to manage. Project two is a set of existing Spark jobs that engineers want to move without rewriting. Which TWO statements about choosing services are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Managed Service for Apache Spark suits project one because it cannot run existing code, which forces a new design
Managed Service for Apache Spark suits project two because it runs open source Spark jobs with little redevelopment
Pub/Sub suits project two because it is the engine that runs Spark programs
Dataflow suits project two because it executes unmodified Spark programs directly without any translation
Dataflow suits project one because it is fully managed, autoscaling and handles both streaming and batch

stem: An energy utility wants to build an end-to-end solution. Smart meters send readings continuously. The readings must be received reliably, cleaned and aggregated as they arrive, stored for SQL analysis, and shown to managers in dashboards. Which sequence matches the role of each service?

choices.text: Pub/Sub receives the readings, Dataflow cleans them, BigQuery stores them for SQL analysis, Looker presents dashboards
Looker receives the readings, Pub/Sub cleans them, BigQuery presents the dashboards, Dataflow stores them for SQL analysis
BigQuery receives the readings, Looker cleans them, Dataflow stores them, Pub/Sub presents the dashboards
Dataflow receives the readings, Looker cleans them, Pub/Sub stores them, BigQuery presents the dashboards

stem: A regional insurer must add automatic transcription of recorded phone claims to its claims portal before the busy season starts in six weeks. Transcription is a common task, the insurer has no machine learning staff, and the transcripts do not need to be a source of competitive advantage. Which approach best fits these strategic factors?

choices.text: Train a custom speech model from scratch on the insurer's recordings, because only a self-built model can ever be considered accurate
Hire a research team to design a new model architecture first, then decide later whether the portal needs transcription at all
Wait for the busy season to end and then fund a multi-year programme that builds a general-purpose speech platform in-house
Call a pre-trained speech API such as Speech-to-Text, which delivers the capability quickly with little development effort or ML expertise

stem: A specialty lender holds fifteen years of its own repayment histories and believes that a model trained on this data would predict defaults better than any competitor's generic tool. Leadership accepts a longer project to gain an advantage that rivals cannot copy. Which factor most strongly argues for a custom model on Agent Platform rather than a ready-made API?

choices.text: Reduced expertise, because custom training on proprietary data removes any need for data preparation or for evaluating results
Speed, because training a custom model always finishes faster than calling a service that already exists and is ready to use
Differentiation, because a model trained on proprietary data can capture patterns that a generic pre-trained service cannot offer to competitors
Uniformity, because every competitor using the same generic service would then get identical predictions, which the lender prefers because it makes outcomes easy to compare

stem: A mail-order retailer keeps customer purchase records in tables. It wants to predict which customers are likely to stop buying, but it has no data scientists and no one who writes training code. The retailer is willing to prepare a labelled dataset. Which Google Cloud approach fits best?

choices.text: AutoML on Agent Platform, which trains a prediction model from labelled tabular data without requiring code or deep data-science skills
Speech-to-Text, which converts customer call audio into text transcripts but does not train on purchase records or make predictions
Cloud Translation, which converts the text of customer messages from one language to another but does not predict behaviour
Custom training on Agent Platform, in which engineers write a training application and choose algorithms, loss functions and hardware

stem: A grocery chain's data lives in BigQuery. Its analysts are fluent in SQL but do not program in Python or Java, and they want to forecast weekly demand per store without waiting for the engineering team. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: A custom training job on dedicated accelerators, which requires engineers to write and package the training application first
Export every table to spreadsheets, and have each analyst write a forecasting program in a general-purpose language from scratch
BigQuery ML, which lets analysts create and run ML models with standard SQL directly where the data already lives
Cloud Translation, which provides pre-trained language translation and has no ability to forecast numeric demand from sales tables

stem: A data-platform director wants to justify BigQuery ML to the board. Which TWO benefits can she cite? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Every model type is available with unlimited control over the training hardware, including the choice of individual accelerators
Models are built where the data already sits, so there is no need to move and reformat large datasets for separate ML tools
Models trained in BigQuery ML automatically replace all dashboards, removing the need for any business intelligence tools
Warehouse data is first copied into a separate ML platform, and the models are returned to BigQuery after a manual review
Data analysts can build and run models with SQL skills they already have, without writing Python or Java ML code

stem: A global furniture seller wants its support site to show product manuals and customer notices in the shopper's own language. The content changes weekly and the seller wants the least possible build effort. Which Google Cloud AI service matches?

choices.text: Speech-to-Text, a pre-trained service that turns spoken audio into text but does not render written content in other languages
AutoML tabular training, which builds prediction models from labelled rows and columns and has no function for converting languages
Cloud Vision, a pre-trained service that analyses images to detect labels and text but does not translate written content
Cloud Translation, a pre-trained service that translates text and documents between many languages through an API

stem: A used-car marketplace receives photographs from sellers and wants to automatically read licence-plate text and flag photos that contain unwanted content before publishing. The team wants a ready-made capability, not a model project. Which service fits best?

choices.text: BigQuery ML time-series forecasting, which predicts future numeric values and does not analyse photographs
Cloud Translation API, which converts text from one language to another but does not analyse the content of photographs
Cloud Vision API, which analyses images with pre-trained models to detect text, labels and explicit content
Speech-to-Text, which transcribes audio recordings and cannot examine the pixels of an uploaded photograph

stem: A hotel group's front desk wants one assistant that can read a guest's typed question, look at a photo of a damaged item the guest sends, and draft a polite written reply. Which kind of Google Cloud AI is the best match for this mix of inputs and outputs?

choices.text: A multimodal foundation model such as Gemini, which can understand text and images together and generate written responses
A translation-only API, which converts text between languages but cannot interpret photographs or compose new messages
A speech-only API, which transcribes audio but cannot interpret typed questions or photographs
A tabular AutoML model, which predicts one outcome from labelled rows and does not write replies

stem: A chief information officer asks colleagues to explain, in one sentence, what Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform offers a company that wants to use AI on Google Cloud. Which description is most accurate?

choices.text: A physical data-centre appliance that runs on the customer's premises and cannot be reached from any Google Cloud service
A single prebuilt application for answering employees' e-mail, with no way to choose models or to build anything custom
A spreadsheet add-on for formatting cells that is sold separately from other Google Cloud products and has no model catalogue or ML tooling
A managed platform to find and use models, build and deploy agents and apps, and train and manage custom ML models across their lifecycle

stem: A product manager at a publisher wants to try out different instructions and models for a summarising feature, and wants to share working prototypes with colleagues who do not write code. Which Agent Platform tool suits this?

choices.text: A data-warehouse export job, which copies tables to cloud storage but does not provide any way to prototype with models
Agent Studio, which provides a low-code environment for designing and prototyping with models and agents without writing code
A hardware reservation for accelerator clusters, which provides computing capacity but no way to design or share prototypes
A raw training cluster for custom models, which requires engineers to write and run a training application first

stem: A manufacturer must classify photos of its own parts as "pass" or "defect". Option one is AutoML with labelled photos from its production line; option two is custom training by a small ML engineering team. The classification goal is standard and the team is small, but later it may want a special loss function. Which comparison guides the decision best?

choices.text: AutoML can target any objective and supply any loss function, so custom training is never needed for any business problem
Custom training is faster and needs no expertise, while AutoML requires its users to write their own training application and algorithms
AutoML and custom training differ only in price, since both need an identical amount of expertise, code and time to produce a first model
AutoML gets a model faster with less expertise but only for predefined objectives, while custom training allows any objective at greater effort

stem: A media group wants a summarising feature, but its leadership worries about depending on a single model supplier: the best model for this task may change within a year, and the group wants to switch without rebuilding the application. Which strategic factor and Google Cloud capability address this?

choices.text: Technical expertise, because only a self-managed on-premises server room can hold more than one model at the same time
Choice and flexibility, using Model Garden on Agent Platform to try and switch among Google, partner and open models
Differentiation, because every company that uses the same single model automatically obtains a unique competitive advantage
Implementation speed, because a single fixed model is always the fastest to adopt and removes any later need to compare models

stem: A regional clinic wants to turn recorded dictation into text notes. A consultant proposes first buying a large cluster of accelerators on AI Hypercomputer so that the clinic can train its own speech model. The clinic has no ML staff and no wish to compete on speech technology. What is the soundest advice?

choices.text: Use a pre-trained speech API first; AI Hypercomputer is for organizations that train and serve large models themselves and need that scale
Cancel the project, because dictation transcription cannot be done on Google Cloud without training a model
Proceed with the cluster, because any AI workload on Google Cloud must run on AI Hypercomputer before an API can be called
Proceed with the cluster, because training a speech model internally is always faster than calling an existing service

stem: A marketing agency is choosing how to get product-description writing. One idea is to call Gemini with carefully written instructions. Another is to train a language model. The agency has few examples, a two-week deadline and needs good-enough quality. Which TWO statements are the sound reasoning? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Prompt-based use rules out ever improving quality afterwards, because a foundation model cannot be adapted to a specific business task
Training a language model from scratch is the quickest option because it removes any need for large datasets or computing power
A foundation model can be steered by prompts, which is the quickest route and needs no training data or model-building skills
Choosing a foundation model removes the agency's choice of models, because the platform contains only a single model
If prompting later falls short, tuning on its own examples can raise quality for the specific task, so the agency can escalate when needed

stem: Nine months ago an airline began building its own translation model for customer notices. The project is late, needs constant maintenance, and quality is no better than commercial services. Notices are ordinary written text, and the airline wants service restored quickly. What should leadership conclude?

choices.text: Translation requires a speech model, so the project should switch to Speech-to-Text before any further investment
The task is a commodity, so adopting Cloud Translation would have given faster results with far less effort and expertise
The airline should add a second custom model for the same task, since two models always cost less than one managed API
The team needs more training data and more accelerators, because a custom model is always the correct choice for translation

choices.text: Stop using AI for inspection and ask suppliers to describe each fault in written reports that the quality team reads
Replace the image service with Cloud Translation so that the fault names are standardized across languages
Train a custom image model on the labelled fault photos, for example with AutoML on Agent Platform, to learn the plant's specific defects
Keep relying on the generic service and add more people to review every photo it labels by hand

stem: A utility's contact centre records thousands of calls a day. Managers want searchable text of each call and a short summary of the customer's issue. Which combination of Google Cloud AI offerings fits?

choices.text: Speech-to-Text to turn the audio into transcripts, then a Gemini model to summarize each transcript into the customer's issue
Cloud Vision API to read the audio files as images, then Cloud Translation to shorten the readable text into a summary
Gemini alone, with the audio discarded after each call so that only the managers' own written notes are summarized
BigQuery ML forecasting to turn the audio into text, then AutoML tabular training to write the summary of each call

stem: A national retailer wants analysts to classify thousands of customer reviews stored in BigQuery as positive, neutral or negative and then report counts by product, using the skills the analysts already have. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Build and host a new custom language model on dedicated accelerators before any analysis can begin
Export the reviews into e-mail attachments and have managers read and tag each review by hand every month
Use Cloud Translation to convert the reviews into another language, since translation also scores the feelings in the text
Use BigQuery ML from SQL to call a Gemini model or a Cloud AI API over the review text and store results in a table

stem: A bank's data-science group wants one governed environment to prepare datasets, train custom models, deploy them to production and keep them under control, plus a catalogue of ready models to try. Which TWO capabilities of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform match this? (Select TWO)

Managed datasets with AutoML and custom training, so the group can build models from its own data and manage them across their lifecycle
A billing statement printer that formats invoices, which is unrelated to datasets, models or deployment tooling
A consumer photo-sharing service for uploading holiday pictures, with no tools for datasets, training or deployment
Model Garden, a library to discover, test and deploy Google, partner and open models without leaving the platform

stem: A retailer has three AI requests: (1) a forecast of weekly store demand from warehouse tables, built by SQL-fluent analysts; (2) captions for product photos with no training project; (3) a model for a unique, patented sorting objective needing its own loss function. Which pairing is the best fit?

choices.text: AutoML for the patented objective, because AutoML can target any objective that a company can describe in writing
A pre-trained translation API for all three requests, since one service is simpler to explain to the board
Custom training for the forecast, BigQuery ML for the photo captions, and a pre-trained service for the patented sorting objective as well
BigQuery ML for the forecast, a pre-trained vision or Gemini service for captions, and custom training on Agent Platform for the unique objective

stem: A manufacturer must leave its data center this year. Its production-planning software is a vendor package that needs a specific operating system, a licensed agent and administrator access to the machine, and the vendor will not support a rewrite. Which Google Cloud product gives the manufacturer the fastest path with the least change to the software?

Apigee, which publishes and secures APIs in front of backend services but does not host the vendor package itself
Compute Engine, which runs VMs where the company picks the operating system and keeps administrator control

stem: A finance firm's risk team runs workloads of very different sizes. Some need many CPUs but little memory, others need large memory, and one team wants GPUs for model training. Leadership wants to avoid buying fixed server models. Which TWO statements describe the business value Compute Engine offers here? (Select TWO)

stem: An airline's booking software is one large application. Changing the baggage-fee rules forces a full release of everything, so new features reach customers only twice a year. The CTO wants features released independently and failures in one area not to bring down the rest. What business value does a microservices architecture offer for this goal?

choices.text: The application becomes a single deployable unit, so there is only one release to test and one place where a failure can occur

The number of teams needed falls to one, because a single group must own every service to keep them consistent
Hardware is no longer needed to run the application, because services are described as code and run without any compute resources at all

stem: A startup's three developers want to launch a customer-facing app within weeks. They would rather not build their own database operations, authentication and messaging systems. Which TWO statements describe how managed services accelerate this goal? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Managed services remove the need to design the application, because Google chooses the business logic on the startup's behalf
Managed services guarantee that the startup will never pay for any resource, because Google absorbs the operating costs
Google runs the underlying operations such as patching, backups and scaling, so developers spend their time on features rather than plumbing
Managed services are only available for workloads that are first rewritten as VMs with the startup's own operating system images

stem: A ticket retailer buys enough servers to survive a once-a-year sale, so most of the year the hardware sits mostly idle. The CFO wants spending to follow demand while the site still copes with the peak. Which modern application development approach addresses both goals?

choices.text: Run on elastic managed platforms that scale out when traffic rises and scale back when it falls, so cost follows actual use
Move the application to one very large server, so that only a single machine has to be paid for, patched and monitored
Provision the peak capacity permanently on virtual machines, so that the site never has to scale and cost stays predictable
Cap traffic at the average level during the sale, so that the existing servers are enough and no extra capacity is ever needed

stem: A logistics company has packaged dozens of services as containers. Its engineers want Kubernetes features such as rolling updates and automatic restarts, but they do not want to build or operate the Kubernetes control plane themselves. Which Google Cloud product fits?

choices.text: Cloud Storage, which stores the container images as objects but does not schedule, scale or restart running containers
Compute Engine alone, where the company installs and upgrades Kubernetes itself on its own virtual machines
Looker, which analyzes the performance data of the services but does not run containers

stem: Two platform teams use GKE. The first employs experienced Kubernetes engineers who must tune node hardware, networking and scheduling for specialized workloads. stem: A media company packaged its web application as a container. Traffic is unpredictable: it spikes during live events and drops to nothing overnight. The company wants to pay only while requests are being handled and has no staff to manage servers or clusters. Which product best fits?

choices.text: GKE Standard, where the team sizes, upgrades and monitors node pools to match the changing traffic by itself
Cloud Run, a serverless platform that runs containers, scales with requests including down to zero and charges for use
Cloud Storage, which hosts static files cheaply but does not run an application container

stem: An online photo service wants small pieces of code to run automatically each time a customer uploads a picture, for example to create a thumbnail and record it in a database. The team does not want to run any servers or keep anything idle in between uploads. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: A GKE cluster sized for the busiest hour of the year, so that every upload is handled by a node that was already running

Cloud Run functions, where a small piece of code runs in response to an event and the team pays only while it executes

stem: A retailer is choosing a home for three workloads. Workload 1 is a legacy package that needs its own operating system. Workload 2 is a set of many containerized microservices that need fine control over networking and scheduling. stem: A product owner is asked to summarize the business value of serverless computing on Google Cloud for the leadership team. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The business must size and patch the underlying servers itself, which gives it the most hardware control

stem: A consultancy holds customer data in Amazon S3 and in Azure Blob Storage. Its analysts know BigQuery and want to query that data with BigQuery SQL from one interface, without copying everything into Google Cloud first. Which product supports this?

choices.text: Cloud Run functions, which would need custom code to copy the data into one bucket before analysis
BigQuery Omni, which runs BigQuery analytics on data stored in Amazon S3 or Azure Blob Storage
Compute Engine, which hosts virtual machines where analysts would install their own query tools on each cloud
