A folder for the retail division that holds the projects, with the policy set at the folder so it flows down to them
A separate billing account for every project, since a billing account carries the security and access rules of the projects that are linked to it
The individual resources inside each project, such as every virtual machine and every storage bucket, configuring the policy on each of them separately

stem: A multinational has hundreds of projects owned by many teams and wants the Google Cloud resource hierarchy to help with governance. Which TWO benefits does the hierarchy provide? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Policies set on a folder are permanently locked once saved and cannot be changed by anyone, including the people who are responsible for them
Every project automatically receives identical built-in spending limits from its parent, so the company never needs to create budgets or quotas
Access control and policies set high in the hierarchy are inherited by the resources below, which keeps security and compliance consistent
Resources in different projects of the organization are blocked from communicating with each other under any circumstances once the hierarchy exists
A single organization-level view lets auditors and administrators see and review the projects, folders and resources in the company

stem: A team configures a budget for its project with alert threshold rules at 50, 90 and 100 percent. After the project passes 100 percent of the budget, the team is surprised that its applications keep running and no services have been shut off. What is the most likely explanation?

choices.text: A budget with threshold rules is alerts-only: it notifies recipients as spend crosses percentages and does not itself stop resources
Google Cloud ignores budgets for any project that uses more than one service, so the threshold alerts never applied to this project
Threshold rules only start working after an administrator manually approves each alert, so the project was not yet being watched by the budget
The budget was misconfigured, because a budget always disables the whole project and all its services once the final threshold is reached

stem: A startup is worried that a coding mistake, or stolen credentials, could create thousands of virtual machines overnight and produce a very large bill. It wants a built-in safeguard that limits how many resources a project can consume, not just a notification afterwards. Which control fits?

choices.text: A resource quota on the project, which restricts how much of a resource it can use and blocks consumption beyond that
A longer approval workflow in which finance signs every invoice before the payment is made to Google
A larger billing account, since bigger accounts automatically refuse any request for more than the average level of resource use
A weekly Cloud Billing report that the finance manager reads on Monday morning to look for anything unusual in the past week of spending

stem: A media company runs a large video-rendering job every night. The job is split into many independent pieces that can be retried, and the deadline is the next morning, so a few interrupted pieces only cause a delay. The company wants to reduce compute cost. Which approach best balances cost and risk?

choices.text: Run the job on Spot VMs and also host the company's always-on customer payment service on them to save more
Buy a permanent fleet of standard VMs sized for the nightly peak, and leave them running all day and night to avoid any interruption
Cancel the nightly job and render each video only when a customer asks for it, regardless of how long that customer must then wait
Run the job on Spot VMs, accepting that capacity may be reclaimed, because the work is fault-tolerant and restartable

stem: An AI research team needs accelerators (GPUs) for a training run that can start whenever capacity becomes available. Capacity for these high-demand resources is scarce, and the finance lead does not want to pay for reserved hardware that sits idle while the team waits. Which Google Cloud approach fits?

choices.text: Ask for a permanent standard reservation of the maximum GPU capacity the team could ever need and keep it for all months of the year
Use the Dynamic Workload Scheduler, which provisions scarce GPUs and TPUs when available, so the team need not hold idle hardware
Run the training on Spot VMs only, since they are the cheapest option
Buy GPUs outright, install them in the company's own server room and depreciate the purchase over several years

stem: A software company runs its application in production. Developers see that the application is slow and want to find which functions and lines of code use the most CPU and memory while real users are on the service. Which Google Cloud Observability tool should they use?

choices.text: Cloud Trace, which follows a single request as it passes through several services
Error Reporting, which groups application crashes so the team can see how many different problems exist and whether each is new
Cloud Profiler, which gathers CPU and memory use from production and ties it to the code that uses it
Cloud Logging, which stores the text messages produced by the application and the platform

stem: An online store built from several microservices receives complaints that checkout is slow. No service reports errors and all of them look healthy individually. The operations lead wants to see how long a single customer request spends in each service it passes through, to find the slowest step. Which tool fits best?

choices.text: Cloud Trace, which follows a request across services and shows how much latency each step adds
Error Reporting, because slow checkout is an error that it would group by root cause
A weekly cost report, because slow requests always mean the services were expensive to run
Cloud Profiler, because it shows how much CPU each service uses over the whole week

stem: After a new release, an application throws a mix of exceptions. The development manager wants a view that shows which kinds of errors are happening, how often each occurs and when a new type first appears, rather than reading thousands of raw messages. Which tool provides this?

choices.text: Cloud Profiler, which shows where the code spends its CPU time and memory rather than listing and grouping exceptions
Error Reporting, which aggregates application error events into groups by root cause and lets teams triage them
Cloud Trace, which charts request latency but does not categorize exceptions
Cloud Monitoring uptime checks, which only report whether the website responded to probes sent from various locations

stem: An operations director wants two capabilities: a chart plus an automatic notification to the on-call team whenever the average response time rises above an agreed level, and a searchable record of exactly what each application and the platform did around the time of an incident. Which combination of tools matches these needs?

choices.text: Cloud Profiler for the notification, and Error Reporting for the searchable record of every event and message
Cloud Logging for the chart and the notification, and Cloud Monitoring for the searchable record of events and messages
Cloud Monitoring for the chart and alerting policy, and Cloud Logging for the searchable record of events
Cloud Trace for both, because traces store metrics and event text in the same place

stem: A CIO asks the cloud team to explain what operational excellence means for the company's cloud workloads and what it relies on. Which statement matches Google's description?

choices.text: Keeping every operation manual and approved by a single senior engineer, so that each change is checked by hand
Reaching a state in which no incident ever occurs, after which the monitoring tools can safely be switched off
Buying the most expensive infrastructure available so that no workload ever needs maintenance or monitoring again
Operating workloads efficiently through automation, orchestration and data-driven insights, with continuous learning

stem: A bank states that its payments service must keep working for customers even if one server or one building fails, and that it must also consistently do what customers expect. Which pair of terms describes these two goals?

choices.text: High availability for staying up through a component failure, and reliability for consistently doing its job
Latency for staying up through the failure of a component, and saturation for consistently doing its job
Scalability for staying up through the failure of a component, and quota for consistently doing its job
Reliability for staying up through the failure of a component, and capital expenditure for consistently doing its job

stem: A healthcare provider is designing a patient-records system on Google Cloud that must keep running if a failure affects one location and must not lose records. Which TWO design approaches support this? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Turn off monitoring in production to avoid noise, since failures will be reported by users
Replicate data to another location and keep regular backups that can be restored
Size the system for today's load only and add capacity manually when users complain about slowness
Place the application and its only copy of the data on one large server, which is simpler to manage
Run redundant copies of the application in more than one zone, or region, so that another copy can serve users if one fails

stem: A team replicates its customer database to a second region in real time. An employee mistakenly deletes an important table. The manager is surprised that the second region does not hold the table either. What does this show?

choices.text: Backups and replication are exactly the same thing, so adding backups would not have changed the outcome
The replication was set up incorrectly, because a correct replica always keeps old data after a delete
Replication is useful only to reduce running costs, so it was never meant to help in this kind of situation at all
Replication protects against a site failure but copies mistakes too, so backups are also needed to restore deleted data

stem: An operations team uses the four golden signals to monitor a web service: latency, traffic, errors and saturation. During a sales event the team sees that memory use and the request queue are close to the limits of what the service can handle, although response times are still normal. Which signal is this, and what does it warn about?

choices.text: Latency, because it shows how long users must wait for responses and whether they are already slow
Errors, because it counts the requests that have already failed with an error code returned to users
Saturation, because it shows how full the service is and warns of nearing capacity before users are affected
Traffic, because it measures how many requests the service receives each second during the sales event

stem: An online ticket seller wants alerts that reflect what customers actually experience, rather than internal machine statistics. Which TWO of the following best show that customers are being harmed? (Select TWO)

choices.text: The number of employees on the on-call rota, because more people on call means fewer customer errors
The total number of log lines produced, because more logs always mean more customers
Rate of errors, because failed requests mean customers cannot complete their purchases
Saturation of the build servers used by developers, because their load decides customers' wait time
Latency of requests, because slow responses frustrate customers even when the service is technically up

stem: A software provider sells a hosted service to business customers. Its engineers track the percentage of successful requests every day. The leadership sets an internal target of 99.95 percent. The contract with customers promises 99.9 percent per month, with service credits if the provider misses it. Which statement maps these three items to SRE terms correctly?

choices.text: The measured success percentage is the SLI, the 99.95 percent target is the SLO and the contract promise with credits is the SLA
The measured success percentage is the SLO, the 99.95 percent target is the SLA and the contract promise with credits is the SLI
The measured success percentage is the SLA, the 99.95 percent target is the SLI and the contract promise with credits is the SLO
All three are SLAs, because each of them is a number related to availability

stem: A home-improvement retailer wants independent software vendors and partner agencies to build apps on top of its product-catalog APIs. Today each partner emails the IT team to learn how the APIs work and to get access credentials, and onboarding takes weeks. Which capability of Apigee API Management addresses this most directly?

choices.text: A container platform that runs every partner's application inside the retailer's own clusters so that the IT team controls the partner code
An API proxy layer that copies the catalog database into each partner's own project so that partners no longer need to call any of the retailer's APIs
A data warehouse that stores all partner questions and answers so that the IT team can reply to each onboarding email more quickly
A developer portal where partners discover the APIs, read the documentation and register their apps themselves without waiting for the IT team

stem: A bank exposes an account-lookup API to partner fintech companies. One partner's faulty script suddenly sends a huge number of requests and slows the bank's backend system for every other partner. The bank wants to protect the backend without changing the backend code. What should it do?

choices.text: Move the backend system to a larger group of virtual machines so that it can absorb any number of requests from any single partner
Apply traffic-management policies such as rate limits and quotas in the Apigee API proxy layer, so that each partner has its own allowance
Ask every partner to promise in writing that it will not send too many requests, and review the contracts again at the end of each year, trusting that no script will ever misbehave
Remove the API from the partner portal so that no partner can use it until all partners have rebuilt their applications

stem: An executive asks why the company should publish public APIs at all. Which TWO statements describe real business benefits of doing so? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Each published API automatically moves the company's data out of its own control and into the possession of its partners
Publishing an API removes the need for the company to secure or monitor the systems behind it, because the API shields them completely
Public APIs make the company's internal systems identical to those of its partners, which removes all differences between organizations
A stable API lets the company change or modernize its backend systems while apps and partners keep calling the same interface
Partners and developers can build new products on the company's capabilities, which widens its reach and can create revenue through API products

stem: A travel company offers its booking API to many partner websites. The product manager cannot say which partners call the API most, which API versions are still used, or where errors cluster, and therefore cannot decide what to improve or retire. Which Apigee capability answers these questions?

choices.text: A database migration tool, which copies the booking data to a new location so that usage can be counted from the copy
API analytics and monitoring, which show traffic, usage by consumer and error patterns across the company's APIs
A virtual machine image, which captures the server's disk so that engineers can inspect usage on it later
A load balancer, which spreads requests evenly across servers so that every partner receives exactly the same traffic

stem: A film studio renders animated scenes on a render farm that needs specific CPU and memory sizes and GPU accelerators. The studio wants to pick the hardware shape for each job, run licensed rendering software that is installed on a full operating system, and stop paying when a job ends. Which product fits best?

choices.text: Compute Engine, because VMs let the studio choose machine shapes and GPUs, control the operating system, and delete them after use
Cloud Run functions, because small event-driven functions run the rendering software without any operating system or hardware choice to manage
Apigee, because its proxy layer chooses CPU and GPU hardware for each rendering job based on the API calls received
Cloud Storage, because storing the scene files in buckets also performs the rendering calculations without any servers

stem: A retailer's CTO wants to explain what modern application development on Google Cloud gives the business. Which TWO statements are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Moving to the cloud guarantees that an application never fails, so redundancy and monitoring are no longer part of the design
Splitting an application into one large codebase makes each feature faster to release because every team edits the same file
Using managed services lets small teams spend less time on patching and operating infrastructure and more time on features customers see
Managed services remove the need to think about cost, because usage is always free once an application is built from containers
Microservices can be scaled and updated independently, so a busy checkout service can grow without redeploying the whole application

stem: An online payments company receives a notification call from its card processor each time a payment settles. The call must trigger a few lines of code that update an order status. Settlements arrive unevenly through the day and the company does not want to manage servers or pay for idle capacity. Which approach fits best?

choices.text: A dedicated virtual machine in Compute Engine that runs around the clock so that it is always ready for the next settlement
A new on-premises server that the company buys, installs and patches so that it can keep the code close to its own team
Cloud Run functions, because the small piece of code runs only when a request arrives and the platform handles scaling and servers
A self-managed Kubernetes cluster sized for the busiest hour of the year and left running at that size all year long

stem: A regional bank has agreed to migrate to Google Cloud. Its workloads include a customer-facing mobile backend, a payment core and an internal staff-lunch ordering tool. The steering committee wants to build migration skills and confidence before touching critical systems. Which first step is most sensible?

choices.text: Migrate the low-risk internal lunch-ordering tool as a pilot first, learn from it, and then apply the lessons to more critical workloads
Move all workloads on the same weekend so that the bank never has to run two environments in parallel
Delay the migration until every application has been rewritten as microservices, because nothing should move before that
Start with the payment core, because proving the hardest workload first shows the cloud can handle the bank's most valuable system

stem: A gaming company has players in North America, Europe and Asia. It wants one public entry point for the game's web services that sends each player to the closest healthy set of servers and keeps working if one region has a problem. Which capability supports this goal?

choices.text: A nightly backup of the game's data to cheaper storage, which protects data but does not direct player traffic anywhere
Spot VMs, which are discounted machines that can be stopped by Google and therefore help only with cost, not with traffic routing
Autoscaling a single group of servers in one region, which adds machines when load rises but cannot place servers near each player
Global load balancing, which distributes incoming traffic across backends in several regions and routes around unhealthy ones

stem: An employee opens an email attachment that looks like an invoice. Afterward, the employee's computer runs hidden software that records keystrokes and quietly sends them to an outside party. What is the best name for this kind of threat?

choices.text: Data residency, because the company chose to keep information in a particular geographic location
Malware, because software designed to harm or spy on a system was delivered through an attachment and ran without the user's knowledge
A distributed denial-of-service attack, because many sources flood a service with requests until legitimate users cannot reach it
A misconfiguration, because an administrator set a cloud resource up in a way that left it open to the public

stem: A health insurer wants to protect member data in two situations: when records are copied from its branch offices to Google Cloud over the internet, and when the records sit on disks in the cloud. Which TWO protections address these situations? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Encryption in transit, which scrambles data while it moves across the network so that interceptors cannot read it
A public bucket policy, which lets anyone read the files so that the branch offices can fetch them without credentials
Data deletion every hour, which removes the records so that there is nothing left to protect during the transfer
Encryption in use only, which protects the data while a processor is working on it but not while it moves or sits on disk
Encryption at rest, which scrambles stored data so that someone who obtains the disks or files cannot read the contents

stem: A retailer passes its annual compliance audit. Three months later attackers steal customer data through an old, unpatched system that the audit checklist did not cover. A director asks whether passing the audit meant the company was secure. What is the best answer?

choices.text: Yes, because auditors continuously monitor all systems every day and would have blocked the theft in real time
Not necessarily, because compliance shows required controls were met at one point in time, while security is ongoing defense against real threats
No, because compliance and security are the same thing, so the successful theft proves that the audit never took place and that nobody ever checked a control
Yes, because a compliance certificate proves that every possible attack has already been prevented in every system

stem: A hospital reviews three incidents. In the first, a lost laptop exposed patient names. In the second, an error silently altered medication doses in a database. In the third, a ransomware attack made the scheduling system unusable for a day. Which mapping to confidentiality, integrity and availability is correct?

choices.text: All three are confidentiality, because every incident involved patient information being at risk in some way
Lost laptop is integrity, altered doses are availability, and the unusable scheduling system is confidentiality
Lost laptop is confidentiality, altered doses are integrity, and the unusable scheduling system is availability
Lost laptop is availability, altered doses are confidentiality, and the unusable scheduling system is integrity

stem: A contractor signs in to the company's cloud environment with a password and a phone code. When the contractor tries to open the payroll data, access is refused. Later, auditors review a record showing who attempted to open it. Which description matches the three terms?

choices.text: Authentication is the refusal of payroll access, auditing is the sign-in itself, and authorization is the record auditors review later, created only if the contractor were let in
Auditing is the sign-in, authorization is the password and phone code, and authentication is the refusal of payroll access
Authorization is the sign-in, authentication is the refusal of payroll access, and auditing is the password and phone code
Authentication is the sign-in that proves identity, authorization is the refusal for lack of permission, and auditing is the record of who tried

stem: A software company runs a three-tier application in Google Cloud: web servers, application servers and databases. Its security team wants traffic between tiers to be allowed only where the application needs it, using centrally managed rules that can be applied consistently to many resources. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: Spot VMs, which lower the cost of fault-tolerant machines but do not decide which connections are permitted
Looker dashboards, which show charts of the traffic between tiers but cannot allow or block any of it
Cloud Storage storage classes, which move rarely used objects to cheaper storage and never decide which network connections are permitted
Cloud NGFW firewall policies, which define allow and deny rules for network traffic and apply them consistently across resources

stem: After a sensitive dataset was changed, the security lead asks: who made the change, on which resource and at what time? The company wants Google Cloud to answer such "who did what, where and when" questions for investigations and audits. Which capability provides this?

choices.text: Apigee analytics, which report how partner applications use published APIs but not who changed cloud resources
Cloud Audit Logs in Cloud Logging, which record administrative activities and resource access across Google Cloud services
A load balancer, which spreads user traffic across servers but does not keep a record of administrative actions
Cloud Storage Archive class, which keeps rarely read data at low cost for long periods but does not record who changed resources

stem: A company hosts its development, testing and production applications in Google Cloud. Security wants the networks of these environments to be logically separated, with private IP addressing and control over what can connect to what. Which Google Cloud service provides these networking building blocks?

choices.text: Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), which provides logically isolated networks with private addressing, routes and firewall rules
Cloud Run functions, which run small pieces of code and scale with the requests they receive, but do not define separate networks for each environment
Dynamic Workload Scheduler, which obtains accelerators for batch jobs but does not isolate environments
Looker, which presents business intelligence charts but does not provide networks or traffic controls

stem: A regulated customer asks how Google protects the servers themselves before any customer workload runs on them, because attackers can target the boot process and hardware supply chain. Which statement reflects Google's approach?

choices.text: Google relies only on perimeter firewalls, so the servers themselves are not specially protected from tampering
Google disables all logging on the servers so that attackers cannot find out anything about the infrastructure
Google designs its own server boards and network gear, vets component vendors, and uses secure boot so servers start only the intended software
Google rents ordinary servers from outside vendors and leaves it to each customer to check the boot software on them, with no controls of its own over the hardware supply chain

stem: A software company runs a customer database and application servers that need to stay on for at least the next three years at a steady, predictable level. The finance team wants to lower the unit cost of this baseline capacity and is willing to plan ahead. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Committed use discounts, in which the company agrees to a defined amount of resource use for a period in exchange for a lower cost
Moving the data to Archive storage, because rarely accessed storage is the cheapest place for a live database
Cancelling all quotas, so that the servers can grow without limit and the finance team never needs to plan capacity
Spot VMs for the database, because Google may stop them at any time, which is acceptable for a steady customer-facing database

stem: A company shares one Google Cloud billing account among marketing, logistics and research. Finance wants to charge each department for its own cloud use and analyze spend with SQL and dashboards. Which approach supports this best?

choices.text: Give each department a separate credit card so that the cloud provider sends them independent bills with no shared data
Organize resources into projects and labels per department, and export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery to allocate cost by department
Stop using cloud services and return to buying servers, because shared costs cannot be assigned to departments in the cloud and on-premises costs never need to be shared
Use one project for everything and ask departments to estimate their use by hand at the end of the year

stem: A company wants to lower its cloud spend without hurting customers. Which TWO actions are cost-saving practices that fit their intended use? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Run the customer-facing payment database on Spot VMs, since customers rarely mind when the service pauses suddenly
Disable budgets and alerts so that teams are not distracted by spending notices during the quarter
Run fault-tolerant, restartable batch jobs on Spot VMs, accepting that Google may stop machines in exchange for lower cost
Keep all development environments running at full size around the clock so that nobody has to restart them
Use autoscaling so that the number of servers follows demand instead of staying sized for the busiest day

stem: A service promises 99.9 percent of successful requests in a month as its internal target (SLO). By mid-month it has used little of the allowed failures. The product manager wants to know how to use the remaining allowance. What does the error budget suggest?

choices.text: The error budget is the penalty the customer receives from Google Cloud when the SLO is missed in any month
The error budget is a financial limit on cloud spending, so the team must stop using the service when it is reached
The remaining error budget shows that monitoring can be turned off for the rest of the month, since failures are now permitted and nobody needs to look at dashboards any more
Remaining budget leaves room for reasonable risk, such as faster releases, while a nearly spent budget calls for focusing on reliability

stem: A company runs applications in dozens of projects. When something goes wrong, engineers log in to individual machines and search for text files, and they cannot see what happened across services. Leaders want one place to collect, search and analyze logs from all applications. Which product provides this?

choices.text: Apigee, which manages and secures APIs but does not collect logs from every application in the company
Compute Engine, which provides virtual machines and therefore depends on engineers reading files on each machine
Cloud Storage Coldline class, which stores rarely accessed objects cheaply and cannot be searched by an engineer who needs to follow one request across applications
Cloud Logging, part of Google Cloud Observability, which collects logs from applications and services for central search and analysis

stem: A major outage hits a retailer's checkout. Service is restored, and the CEO asks the SRE lead what should happen next to keep it from happening again. Which practice does Google recommend?

choices.text: Identify the engineer who made the last change and remove that person from the on-call rotation as a deterrent, and warn the rest of the team that mistakes will be punished
Close the incident quietly, because discussing outages with other teams only damages the company's reputation
Hold a post-incident review that documents the timeline, root cause and lessons learned, then act on the recommended improvements
Wait for the next outage and compare it with this one, since a single event cannot show anything useful

stem: A payments company runs its customer portal in one Google Cloud region, spread across several zones. The board now asks for protection against the unlikely event that an entire region becomes unavailable, for example because of a regional disaster. Which approach addresses this requirement?

choices.text: Move the portal's static images to edge locations, so that pages load faster for distant customers
Deploy the portal in two or more regions, so that traffic can be served from another region if one is lost
Add more virtual machines to the existing zones, so that each zone has extra capacity during busy periods
Increase the network bandwidth of the current region, so that more requests can be served each second

stem: A food manufacturer wants real-time quality checks on its factory floor, where a delay of even a second would stop a production line, and its plants have unreliable links to the internet. It also wants to analyze the combined data from all plants in the public cloud and migrate other systems gradually. Which model fits?

choices.text: Hybrid cloud, with time-critical systems staying at the plants and analytics and other workloads running in the public cloud
Public cloud only, because all workloads should run in the provider's regions, including the machines next to the production line
A single private cloud in one data center, because analytics at scale cannot use any service from a public provider
Multicloud with two public providers, because the plants need a second provider rather than any equipment on site

stem: A global retailer decides to use more than one public cloud provider. Which TWO benefits can the retailer reasonably expect from this multicloud approach? (Select TWO)

choices.text: All provider services connect to each other without any design, so data moves freely at no extra effort
Operations become simpler automatically, because every provider uses identical tools, interfaces and security settings
The retailer no longer needs to manage identity, security or cost across its environments
Less dependence on a single vendor, which improves negotiating power and reduces lock-in risk
Each workload can run on the provider whose services best fit it, such as one provider's analytics with another's application platform

stem: A company currently rents virtual machines, installing and patching the operating system and middleware itself. It is considering moving its custom order application to a platform where developers only deploy code. What changes in who does the work?

choices.text: The provider takes over the operating system, runtime and scaling, and the company concentrates on its code and data
The company gives up control of its application code, because platform services require the provider's developers to maintain it
The company still patches the operating system, but the provider now writes the order application code
The company must buy and operate its own servers again, because platforms run only in private data centers

stem: A film studio must send raw footage of several terabytes to a cloud storage service every night. The editor complains that the upload does not finish before morning, although a single small test file arrives almost instantly. Which networking concept is the studio most likely short of?

choices.text: IP address space, meaning the studio has too few addresses to start more than one upload
Bandwidth, meaning the studio's connection cannot carry enough data per second for such large transfers
Latency, meaning the studio's network has too long a delay before the first byte of a small file arrives
DNS, meaning the storage service's name cannot be translated into the correct numeric address

stem: A 200-person law firm wants a ready-made case-management application that its staff can use next week. The firm has no developers and wants no responsibility for servers. The partners ask what they give up by choosing SaaS rather than building their own application. What is the most accurate answer?

choices.text: They own every feature decision, because the provider only supplies computers and cannot influence the software
They must patch the operating system and database themselves, which makes SaaS slower to start than a custom build
They get less control over features and underlying configuration, in exchange for speed and no infrastructure to manage
They give up the ability to use the application from the internet, because SaaS runs only on the office network

stem: A cosmetics company wants to test five new online campaign ideas in one month, keeping only the ones that attract customers. In its data center, every experiment needs servers that take weeks to order, so the team tests one idea per quarter. Which cloud benefit most directly changes this?

choices.text: Agility, because resources can be created in minutes and released when an experiment ends
Standardization, because every experiment must use the same hardware as the previous one
Compliance, because cloud providers automatically certify every campaign under the company's name
Physical security, because the company's own data center would need guards for each experiment

stem: A manufacturer's board has approved a cloud program, but the CIO warns of two challenges that often derail digital transformation. Which TWO are such challenges? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Cloud providers never offer training, so every employee must learn alone without any support
Cloud adoption is possible only for companies that have no existing systems at all
Legacy applications and siloed data can be hard to move, integrate or modernize
Moving to the cloud always requires replacing every customer with new ones
Employees may lack new skills and resist changing working habits, which slows adoption

stem: A regional bank notes that customers now expect to open accounts, track payments and resolve problems through an app at any hour, comparing it with the best digital experiences they have had elsewhere. The bank's leaders ask how to describe this force to the board. Which description fits?

choices.text: A regulatory requirement, because laws require every bank to launch a mobile application
A cost-saving initiative, because digital channels reduce the number of branch employees the bank must hire
A technology limitation, because mobile phones cannot yet support secure banking features
A customer-expectation driver of digital transformation, pushing the bank to modernize how it serves people

stem: An online ticket seller expects demand to be small on most days but to jump tenfold when a popular concert goes on sale, then fall again within hours. Leaders want capacity to follow demand in both directions without staff action. Which cloud characteristic is this, and why does it matter?

choices.text: Fixed capacity, which guarantees the same performance by always running the largest possible environment
Elasticity, which adds resources when demand rises and removes them when it falls, so spending follows usage
Data residency, which keeps the sales records in one country to meet local rules
Portability, which lets the seller copy the application to another provider within a few minutes

stem: A company has different departments that each calculate "monthly revenue" in their own spreadsheets, so leaders see different numbers in every meeting. The company wants all dashboards, whatever tool or team produces them, to use one governed definition of each business metric on top of its data warehouse. Which Google Cloud product fits?

choices.text: Cloud Storage, because it can hold a copy of every department's spreadsheet in one bucket
Looker, because it provides a governed semantic layer where metrics are defined once and reused
Cloud Run, because it hosts a web application in which every department types in its own figures
Pub/Sub, because it delivers revenue events to every department as they happen

stem: A wind-turbine operator wants to avoid costly failures. Each turbine sends vibration readings every second. Today engineers review a weekly report and find problems after a turbine has already broken. What is the main business value of moving to streaming analytics?

choices.text: The weekly report becomes longer, because more historical readings can be stored for each turbine
The operator can stop collecting vibration data, since streaming analytics predicts failures without inputs
Readings can be analyzed as they arrive, so warning signs trigger maintenance before the failure occurs
Turbine readings can be kept off the cloud, because streaming analytics works only on local files

stem: A marketing director defends the plan to give store managers and marketers self-service BI tools instead of routing every question to the central analytics team. Which TWO benefits can she cite? (Select TWO)

choices.text: Decisions are based on shared, current data, which reduces reliance on instinct and stale spreadsheets
Every user automatically sees all data in the company, including data they are not meant to see
Data governance becomes unnecessary, because dashboards check the accuracy of data automatically
The central analytics team can be dissolved, because nobody needs advanced analysis any more
Business users can answer many questions themselves, which shortens the wait from days to minutes

stem: An online retailer's checkout service receives a huge surge of order events during a flash sale. The order-processing and analytics systems cannot always keep pace, and the company does not want the checkout to slow down or lose orders. Which Google Cloud service lets the checkout hand off events reliably while downstream systems consume them at their own pace?

choices.text: Looker, a BI platform that displays orders on dashboards after they are stored
Cloud Storage, an object store that returns each order to the checkout for processing
Spanner, a relational database that processes every analytics query inside the checkout service
Pub/Sub, an asynchronous messaging service that decouples event producers from consumers

stem: A manufacturer's finance application was built for Microsoft SQL Server and the vendor does not support other engines. The manufacturer wants to stop patching database servers and handling backups, but cannot change the application. Which Google Cloud service fits?

choices.text: Bigtable, because it is a wide-column NoSQL database for key-based access
Firestore, because it is a document database for mobile and web applications
Cloud Storage, because it can store the database's files as objects and also run the application's transactions
Cloud SQL, a managed relational database service that supports SQL Server as well as MySQL and PostgreSQL

stem: A pharmaceutical company wants to collect lab instrument files, scanned reports, images and CSV exports from many research sites in one low-cost place before deciding how to analyze them. Researchers will later load selected data into an analytics engine. Which approach fits this stage?

choices.text: Use Bigtable to keep each scan as a row, because it is built for scanned documents
Keep files in Cloud Storage as the raw lake landing zone and load selected data into BigQuery later
Discard unstructured files, and keep only CSV exports, because analytics cannot use other formats
Load every file into a Cloud SQL table first, so that images and scans become rows and columns

stem: A retailer runs its order system on a Cloud SQL database. Every month-end, analysts run very large reports on the same database, and during these hours customers see slow checkouts. The company wants to keep orders fast and still allow heavy reporting. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Send order data to BigQuery for reports, so analytics stop competing with checkout transactions
Ask the analysts to run reports more often, so that each run has less data to read
Stop all reporting at month-end, because relational databases cannot support analytics
Replace the order database with Cloud Storage, because object storage handles reports faster

stem: A telecom company wants to understand its customer data. Which TWO of the following are examples of unstructured data? (Select TWO)

choices.text: A spreadsheet of device serial numbers listed in labeled columns
A table of monthly invoices with fixed columns for customer ID, date and amount
Photographs that technicians take of damaged network equipment
A relational table of plan prices and contract lengths
Recorded audio of customer-service calls

stem: A retailer has customer data in several systems. When a customer changes an address, nobody knows who must correct the other copies, and error reports are passed between departments for months. The chief data officer wants clear accountability for the quality and proper use of each data set. Which governance practice addresses this?

choices.text: Delete older copies each night, so that only the newest version survives
Give every employee write access to every system, so anyone can fix any record immediately
Move all data into one larger spreadsheet that people on every team can edit at once
Assign data owners and stewards accountable for the quality, definitions and use of each data set

stem: A bank's developers have built an AI agent prototype that answers customer questions and calls internal systems. Leaders now want to run it in production for thousands of users, with scaling and monitoring handled for them, and without the team managing servers. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: Agent Runtime on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, a managed environment to deploy and scale agents
Cloud Interconnect, because it links the bank's data center to Google's network with a private connection
Looker, because it is a BI tool that can show charts of agent conversations
Cloud Storage, because the agent can be stored as a file that customers download

stem: A research institute trains very large AI models and worries about slow training, inflexible hardware and rising costs. A consultant describes Google Cloud's AI Hypercomputer. Which TWO statements about it are accurate? (Select TWO)

choices.text: It supports only a single type of chip, so every customer must use the same hardware
It is a cloud-hosted spreadsheet tool that analysts use to prepare charts for executives
It offers flexible ways to consume capacity, which helps the institute match cost to workload needs
It requires a fixed multi-year commitment, so the institute cannot adjust consumption
It combines purpose-built hardware, such as GPUs and TPUs, with open software and frameworks

stem: A law firm's partners spend hours reading long supplier contracts to find key obligations and draft short summaries for clients. They want an AI capability that reads long documents and writes clear summaries and answers to questions about them, quickly and without training their own model. Which fits best?

choices.text: BigQuery ML linear regression, because contract summarization is a numeric forecasting task
A Gemini foundation model, which reads long documents and writes summaries and answers
Cloud Vision API, because it detects objects and text in images rather than reasoning over contracts
A custom image classifier trained with AutoML, using photographs of paper contracts

stem: A newspaper wants every article to be available as spoken audio, so that readers with visual impairments and commuters can listen. The paper has no AI specialists and wants natural-sounding voices in several languages soon. Which Google Cloud capability fits?

choices.text: Text-to-Speech, a pre-trained API that turns written text into spoken audio
Cloud Vision API, because it reads printed text from images of newspaper pages
BigQuery ML, because it can train a model on the article archive to forecast readership trends
Speech-to-Text, because it converts a recorded voice into written transcripts

stem: An energy retailer deployed a custom model that predicts customer churn. For six months it worked well, but its accuracy has fallen as customer behavior and tariffs changed. The data science lead wants a managed way to monitor the model, retrain it on newer data and redeploy it. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Replace the model with a rule list written by hand, which never needs updating
Move the customer data to Cloud Storage, because storage location sets model accuracy
Keep the original model unchanged, since a trained model remains accurate forever
Use the MLOps capabilities of Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform to monitor, retrain and redeploy the model

stem: An online marketplace wants to decide which problem to tackle first with machine learning. Which of the following is best suited to ML rather than to a simple fixed rule or ordinary software?

choices.text: Displaying the company logo at the top of every web page
Sorting an invoice list alphabetically by supplier name
Recommending products to millions of shoppers from patterns in past browsing and buying
Calculating sales tax for every order from a published rate table of fixed percentages

stem: An insurer plans to let an AI agent handle claims end to end. A compliance officer worries about large claims and unusual cases. Which practice best balances efficiency with accountability?

choices.text: Publish the agent's decision logic to customers, which removes any need for internal controls
Automate routine claims, and route large or unusual ones to people for review, with decisions logged
Let the agent approve every claim alone, because human review always makes processing slower
Switch off the agent whenever a claim exceeds a typical amount, so no claim is ever automated

stem: A retail executive looks at a dashboard showing that sales in one region fell sharply last month. Her analyst then examines the data by product, store and promotion to find out why sales fell. Which type of data analytics is the analyst performing?

choices.text: Predictive analytics, which forecasts next quarter's sales using a trained model
Descriptive analytics, which only summarizes what happened without looking at causes
Diagnostic analytics, which investigates the causes of something that has already happened
Prescriptive analytics, which automatically changes store prices without human involvement

stem: A company's staff use a generative AI tool to draft customer replies. One reply confidently described a refund policy that does not exist. Leaders want to keep using the tool. Which action best addresses this business risk?

choices.text: Have people review drafts before sending, and ground the tool in real company policies
Treat every output as correct, because generative AI never makes mistakes about facts or policies
Shorten every reply to one sentence, since fewer words always means fewer errors
Ban all customer communication, since generative AI cannot be used for any text task
